section: 9. Priest's Eyeball Bursts: A Terrifying Incident
description: The priest's single eye bulges, blood vessels rupture, and the eyeball explodes like an overripe berry, spraying yellow-green pus mixed with brain matter, triggering a Sanity Check (SC).

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Count Baldwin placed the falcon back on the gilded perch, suddenly looking up with blue eyes like two frozen amber beads in the candlelight. "My dear friends," his Frankish speech carried the soft accent unique to Bruges, "you must have noticed—certain Venetians are defiling this holy war with filthy heretical methods. My soldiers have become more savage than the Saracens... this is certainly not God's will. I want you to find those maggots who call themselves 'Unfettered Flesh' and deliver their black-magic-stained organs to my poor Melovac. That leper's ship is anchored in the old harbor." The falcon suddenly let out a sharp cry, and the count smiled as he tossed a grape into the cage.

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: (None)

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "As for whether the Doge is aware?" He wiped his fingertips meticulously with a handkerchief. "If you can bring me a list of the cultists... I'll remember that the Abbey of Saint-Denis lacks a set of golden liturgical vessels when distributing the spoils." Count Baldwin's fingers lightly tapped the gilded armrest, his voice suddenly dropping lower, as if even the walls might eavesdrop: "Listen—the alliance between Franks and Venetians is less reliable than a whore hanging from a noose." A smile played on his lips, but his eyes were as cold as a winter sea. "Just yesterday, three Venetian bastards were chopped into mincemeat by our knights in the Hagia Sophia cloister." Henry suddenly snorted with laughter, using his dagger tip to pick at a dried bloodstain on the document. "So you must act like monks at night prayer... find those heretics and send them to meet God—but be sure to choose a moonless night."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Bows head silently. "Yes, my lord."

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: #Silently ponders matters concerning the holy relics.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The monk player7 knows the leper monk Melovac, a renowned scholar of the occult, but he has never boarded the leper ship.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "Yes, my lord" #Bows respectfully, then prepares to take his leave.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Count Baldwin slowly rose, his voice like a dull knife scraping bone: "In the north church at the Forum of Theodosius, there's a Venetian priest locked up, spouting heretical tales. When my men pried open his mouth, he actually claimed those 'Unfettered Flesh' scum had tampered with the Doge's Palace long before the city fell. Go listen to that madman's ravings."

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "Understood, Your Excellency."

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "Understood, Your Excellency." #Prepares to head to the north church.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Just as the three turned to leave, Count Baldwin suddenly tapped the table, the crisp sound echoing in the stone chamber. "One more thing..." His voice remained gentle, yet the candlelight inexplicably dimmed. "According to fleeing Byzantine captives, their emperor released something... from the underground water cavern beneath the square's well before the city fell." The count gently stroked the falcon's feathers: "If you encounter something that takes human form but is not human..." The falcon suddenly let out a shrill cry. "Kill it."

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "Yes, sir."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Also, allow my beloved bard, Bradic, to be your guide." "He awaits you outside the door."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Bows and prepares to leave.

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: #Prepares to exit, greeting the bard at the door.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Bradic leaned casually against a stone pillar outside, plucking his strings with a frivolous melody. His gold-embroidered green coat shimmered in the sunlight like a proud kingfisher. "Aha! My dear butcher friends—" A discordant note suddenly sprang from the strings. "Do you know the last fool who guided led the count's spies into a Venetian slaughterhouse?" He dramatically clutched his chest. "Fortunately, you now have a guide who knows his way around both Constantinople's brothels and churches!" He suddenly leaned close to player6, the smell of alcohol and tobacco wafting over. "But then... if I were to lose even one of these priceless fingers—" His fingertip slid over the amethyst inlaid on the neck of his lute. "Whose skin do you think the count would flay first?"

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Rubs his ears.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "So, where shall we go first?"

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "The church would be a good choice; I haven't done my prayers today."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I think I'll go take a look at the old harbor, my lord."

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "Well, I'll follow the arrangements of you two."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Bradic's strings suddenly emitted a discordant note, and he raised his eyebrows exaggeratedly: "Church? Ha! My dear barbarian sir—" His fingertip traced the row of gems on the lute's neck. "The stained glass of Saint Mary's Church was just removed by the Venetians yesterday, and the crypt of Saint John's Church is now piled with twenty stinking corpses... But then~ if you insist on praying amidst the stench of corpses..." He spun around with a cheeky grin. "I do know of a small chapel near the Forum of Theodosius—the priest there hasn't been hanged yet." "Let's go to the chapel first, follow me!" The bard played a frivolous tune as he led the way. (Alright then.)

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Qiduo received! Continuing to record the horror of the Orient Express for you. Currently, 2286 texts recorded, time elapsed: 12 hours, 57 minutes, 30 seconds. Huh? A piece of paper flew out when opening the file. Your most important task right now is the transition to junior high school.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: April 13, 1204, noon.

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: #Adjusts his personal attire. Although not particularly fond of this bard, he follows closely behind to ensure the safety of this important guest before him.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Bradic led the three around a street corner piled with broken pottery, and the view suddenly opened up—the tall arches of the cistern stood in the sunlight, with several broken Roman columns casting long, slanted shadows. Just as you prepared to hurry across, a heart-wrenching scream came from the direction of the cistern. A blood-soaked Frankish knight was being dragged down the steps by two burly Varangians, his armor scraping harshly against the stone steps, his desperately struggling hands leaving streaks of blood. "Damn! It's those Nordic barbarians!" Bradic grabbed player8's sleeve. "They specifically target those alone—" Before he finished, another Varangian brute emerged from the shadows, his axe blade still dripping blood. He squinted, sizing up the four, and said slowly in Frankish with a Nordic accent: "Masters... want to go for a swim too?"

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: #Frowns slightly, but his hands hang naturally, muscles tensed. His previously casual gaze becomes serious as he places a hand on his sword hilt, preparing to counterattack and defend.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Tries to stand taller, raising his club to shield and cover Eloise behind him.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The Nordic brute grinned, his gold tooth flashing coldly in the sunlight. He slowly spun his battle-axe, blood droplets flicking onto the stone steps. "Oh? The priest wants to play?" he mocked in broken Frankish, his thick fingers rubbing the axe handle. "Perfect, I haven't killed anyone wearing a cross yet." Just as the distance between them closed to within five paces, the dying Frankish knight suddenly surged up—he tore off his blood-soaked cloak, revealing the Varangian's signature chainmail underneath. Simultaneously, two more Nordic warriors armed with short axes, who had been hiding behind stone pillars, rushed out, blocking the retreat. The disguised Frankish knight suddenly rolled forward from the ground, his sword aiming straight for player7's ankle. .ra Brawl 45

conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; if it is what you hope for, it will surely be answered. <player3>'s Brawl 45 prayer: D100=100/45 Critical Failure. img style=max-width: 300px src=data/images/pictures/Critical Failure.jpg / -Maybe try again, can't possibly have two critical failures in a row...

conversation.text: #Smash the club down hard on his head

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The ambusher on the left spread his arms and lunged at player6, trying to grapple with brute force. But the disguised Norseman, who had just rolled halfway, suddenly slipped—he stepped on the fake clothes he had just discarded, lost his balance completely, and his sword blade skewered crookedly into a crack in the stone steps. player7's club came down with a whistling sound. Thud! The dull sound of a skull cracking echoed under the reservoir arch. The Norseman's head exploded like a ripe pumpkin, red and white matter splattering out. Even worse, his headless corpse, as it fell, happened to crash into his comrade who was lunging at player6—Ah!! The Varangian who had charged barehanded was tripped by the corpse, falling face-first heavily onto the edge of the steps. After the crisp sound of a broken nose bridge, he clutched his bleeding face and rolled into the reservoir, splashing up a huge spray of water.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Stunned

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The remaining two Varangians froze on the spot, the gold-toothed leader's battle-axe still raised mid-air, his face splattered with his companion's brains.

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "Sir, you have quite the skill."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The gold-toothed leader's face was still smeared with warm brains, his axe trembling slightly in mid-air. He stared at his companion's body floating in the reservoir, a strange sound between a roar and a sob rumbling in his throat.

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "You two... still continuing?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The three Norsemen quickly swam into the darkness deep in the reservoir, leaving only rippling blood on the water's surface.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Sol...solved?"

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "Yes"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Are we safe?"

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "We are safe, for now."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Bladic stood frozen in place, water dripping from his strings, the hem of his green coat completely soaked. He looked down at the brain matter splattered on his chest, then looked up at the gradually dissipating bloodstain on the water's surface, suddenly shuddering. By the gods... He retched dryly, pointing at the pool with his lute neck, I'll never eat meat pies again in my life!

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Sir, sometimes thinking less is good for your health"

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "The foreigners received the call of Jesus and left, following the commandments laid down by Moses"

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "This is the Lord's judgment."

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Wipe the club, planning to run, this place is not safe to stay

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Sneak away

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "Mm, let's go."

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: (wow)

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The scorching sun baked the Roman colonnades of the square, the air thick with the mixed scent of sweat, wine, and blood. The entire square was like an open-air market, except the currency of trade was violence—Frankish soldiers were tying gilded church doors onto mule carts, several Burgundian knights surrounded an old Greek scholar, forcing him with dagger points to translate a freshly stolen parchment. In the center of the square, three drunken infantrymen were using an icon painting as a target for throwing hatchets. On the steps of the cathedral to the north lay a corpse in purple robes. The cathedral doors were half-open, and from inside came the sound of arguing, rising and falling—it sounded like a group of Venetians and Franks arguing over the ownership of some cargo. Occasionally, the sound of shattering porcelain and muffled curses drifted from the windows. In the northwest corner of the square, several Hospitaller knights tried to stop violence against civilians, but were quickly overwhelmed by more looting soldiers. A chained Byzantine official suddenly broke free and rushed madly towards the bronze bull statue in the center of the square, only to be impaled by a spear halfway.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Glance at the bard

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Bladic suddenly dropped his playful demeanor, straightened his back, and cleared his throat. In the name of the Lionheart and the Fleur-de-lis. The knight in the northwest corner lifted the trapdoor open with a swift motion. After you, sir. He lowered his voice, That Venetian priest is in the third storage room.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Climb into the trapdoor

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The flickering torchlight illuminated the damp basement, mottled walls covered in mold, with moldy bread and overturned wine jugs piled in the corners.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "I must say, you have talents we do not, friend. God needs not only stubborn old men like me, but also spiritual talents like you." #Then climb into the trapdoor

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Cover nose and frown

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The one-eyed Venetian priest was chained to an iron ring on the stone wall, his vestments long torn and tattered, stained with filth and dried blood. His remaining eye was bloodshot, pupils dilated, as he writhed and twisted painfully on the ground, his hands clutching his gray hair as if trying to tear his scalp off. Inhuman moans came from his throat, white foam at the corners of his mouth, and he convulsed violently from time to time, making the chains rattle loudly.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What's wrong with him?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Bradick covered his nose and took half a step back, the lute hitting the stone wall with a dull thud. Tsk, he curled his lip, this old fellow looks like he's been 'specially blessed' by God.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "This isn't normal, is it?"

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "Specifically?"

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: #simply observe the situation

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "Like Jesus nailed to a plank?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Special blessing? Sir, could you please explain?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Bradick shrugged, fingers casually plucking the lute strings: I'm just a lute player, what do I know about theological issues? He gestured with his chin towards the priest, better ask this old gentleman directly—though he looks like he's possessed by a devil now.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #step aside, motioning for Eloise to come forward

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #approach the priest

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The priest's left eye has a crooked black eyepatch, with yellow-green pus seeping from the edges.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The priest suddenly stopped convulsing, his bloodshot eye fixed intently on player6.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "'Unfettered Flesh'... what is it? What do you know? Can you tell us?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Father Agostino struggled to lift his head, a single eye flashing with fear and hatred: 'Unfettered Flesh'... these Venetian demons are plotting conspiracies in the secret chambers of the Governor's Palace... They forged documents, inciting the Crusaders to attack Constantinople...

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "You mean, this war is because of this statue?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Father Agostino let out a hoarse, cold laugh: War? No, child... this catastrophe is just the kindling for them to open the gates of hell. His rotting eyepatch rose and fell with his rapid breathing, that's not a statue at all... but a set of ceramic armor forged from living souls. As long as you wear the corresponding skin... He suddenly coughed violently again, spitting out a clot of black blood, —you can gain divine power.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: (cool)

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Huh??? Is this armor really in Byzantium?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Father Agostino suddenly struggled to prop himself up, the iron chains clanking: Ramadi... that Venetian knight... A complex emotion flashed in his remaining eye, he sent us to search the entire city for two things—

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "How do you know all this in such detail? And... your current condition..."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: A cursed suit of armor made of black ceramic... and a Latin ritual scroll hidden by the Byzantines... His fingers dug into the cracks of the stone wall, I heard that scroll records how to destroy the 'Devil's Effigy'... because their ancestors once fought against this evil object...

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #dumbfounded

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "Tsk..." Need to hurry.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Father Agostino's pupils suddenly contracted: They... must still be guarding there... With every word, bloody foam bubbled out, those blue-robed demons... like spiders guarding their webs... lurking in the shadows of the Church of Saint Mokios...
